summary: Full backend + frontend E2E test of Practical Poker Plus. Backend: 17/17 pytest cases passed (auth, coach logins, admin login, /auth/me bearer, coaches list, deck generate via Claude Sonnet 4.6 with varied layouts, list/get/patch deck title, layout swap, PPTX & PDF export producing valid files, upload .txt flow, replay create/get, GIF & MP4 export). Frontend: Login (valid + quick logins + invalid error), Dashboard, Content Studio paste-generate flow (AI produced 9 slides, 10 layouts available), layout switch, deck title save, PPTX+PDF download from browser, Replayer full flow (seat count change, hero hole cards via CardPicker, board picker with used-card disabling verified, deal flop/turn, add bet action, playback controls, save, reload from dashboard restores config, GIF+MP4 exports downloaded).

issues: React console warning: 'Cannot update a component while rendering a different component' triggered by `if (user) navigate('/')` called during Login render (Login.jsx line 21). Should be wrapped in useEffect or use <Navigate/>. Functional but noisy.

action_items: Minor: Fix Login.jsx line 21 - move `if (user) navigate('/')` into useEffect or replace with <Navigate to='/'/> to silence React setState-in-render warning.
Minor cleanup: `activePlayers` variable in Replayer.jsx is computed but never used.
critical_code_review_comments: Login.jsx calls navigate() synchronously during render (line 21) — causes React warning. Wrap in useEffect.
Cookie set with samesite='none' and secure=True — correct for cross-origin, but relies on HTTPS (fine on preview URL).
seed_admin/coaches on startup: admin block resets password if mismatched but coaches always overwrite metadata (not password) — password rotation would require manual reseed. Acceptable for MVP.
MongoDB _id properly excluded from responses via projections {'_id': 0}. bson.ObjectId not leaked.
No rate limiting / brute force lockout on /auth/login — playbook mentions 5-fail lockout expected; not implemented. Not a blocker for MVP but flag for hardening.
server.py is 370 lines — still under the 700-line split threshold; fine.
